title: Shengdana Chutney
name: Maharashtrian Shengdana Chutney
subtitle: A quick, coarse roasted-peanut chutney powder — sprinkle it dry, or loosen it with curd or oil.

method.title: Roast and skin the peanuts
items: In a tawa or skillet on medium heat, roast {@peanuts} 7–8 min, until the skins turn papery and start falling off and the nuts get dark brown spots
Take them off the heat and cool on a tray — a running fan speeds this up
Once cool, rub them between your hands to loosen the skins, then dust or blow the skins off
In the same pan, warm {@oil} if using; add {@red-chilies} and {@hing} for 20–30 sec — deeper flavour — then cool

method.title: Grind and store
items: Put {@peanuts|the skinned peanuts} in the medium jar of a grinder with {@cumin}, {@salt} and {@turmeric}; pulse a few times to rough chunks
Set aside her share now (see the toddler box)
Add the bloomed spice mix {from Step 1} and {@deggi-mirch}; grind further to a grainy powder
Stop before it clumps and releases its oils
Store in a clean jar in the fridge; keeps 3–4 weeks

method.label: Toddler note
items: Before the chilies go into the jar, take {=¼ cup} of the plain peanut powder for her and keep it in a small jar
Stir 1 tsp of it into her curd rice, dal or ghee-rice; it's ground fine enough to be safe — never give her whole peanuts

method.label: Tip
method.text: Garlic → hing, bloomed with the chilies. Variations: add dry-roasted coconut, curry leaves, sesame, coriander seeds or mustard seeds. To use it 'wet', mix 2 tbsp with curd or a little oil.
